$comment: Written counts that are correct even though they disagree with the registry.
A bare number beside a noun is ambiguous: '5 Treatises' can count one
section rather than the corpus, and prose about a past mistake has to quote
the wrong number to make its point.
Each entry needs a file, a distinctive string, and a reason. Matching is on
content, not line number, so an exception survives edits above it. An entry
with an empty reason is ignored, so every exception is a stated decision.
Code comments are skipped wholesale and need no entry here.

allowed.reason: Counts the five papers in that one section, not the corpus. The component holds its own list of PAPER I through PAPER V and never reads the registry.

allowed.match: advertised 25 treatises while the real figure had climbed to 59
allowed.reason: Quotes a past defect to explain why the count gate exists. Correcting the number would delete the lesson.

allowed.match: translating 46 treatises is a content project
allowed.reason: Prose about translation scope written at 46 documents. Stale, but it is describing a deferred content project rather than advertising the corpus size; left for whoever revisits that decision.
